factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of comprehensive income shows Q4 2025 revenue of €60,615k vs €45,203k (2024). Gross margin calculation confirms 5.9% (2025) vs 9.0% (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Operating profit was €0.90 million, compared with €1.09 million, and the group reported a quarterly loss of €0.04 million versus a profit of €0.62 million in the fourth quarter of 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of comprehensive income shows Q4 2025 operating profit of €895k vs €1,089k (2024), and profit for the period of €(43)k vs €618k.

factual_claims.claim: The Estonian construction market stabilised and activity improved somewhat in the second half of the year, while the construction price index rose 1.5%, primarily due to higher material prices.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key figures section states the market stabilised with increased activity in H2 and a 1.5% construction price index rise driven by material prices.

factual_claims.claim: Competition remained strong and public investment in buildings and roads continued to influence demand.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operations and outlook by market section discusses strong competition and the influence of public investment on demand.

factual_claims.claim: Nordecon's order book nevertheless increased approximately 30% to €273.1 million at year-end.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section states the order book stood at €273,060k at 31 December 2025, a ~30% increase from 2024.

factual_claims.claim: New contracts totalled €235.0 million, supported by major Rail Baltica and road-construction contracts.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section reports new contracts secured in 2025 were €234,994k and specifically lists Rail Baltica and road contracts.

factual_claims.claim: Infrastructure represented 42% of the backlog, up from 18%, while Buildings represented 58%, down from 82%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book breakdown table shows Infrastructure at 42% and Buildings at 58% as of 31 December 2025, compared to 18% and 82% in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Management expects business volumes to increase in 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section states management expects business volumes to increase in 2026 based on the order book size and market outlook.

factual_claims.claim: Operating cash flow was €1.20 million, compared with €1.08 million in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of cash flows shows net cash from operating activities of €1,204k (2025) vs €1,075k (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Cash decreased to €5.27 million from €8.20 million, partly reflecting €2.90 million placed in long-term deposits, and the current ratio was 0.93.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash and cash equivalents were €5,266k (2025) vs €8,195k (2024). Cash flows from investing activities note €2,898k placed in long-term deposits. Liquidity risk section states current ratio of 0.93 as of 31 December 2025.
